chains.element: Intergenic site; no overlapping cCRE is reported.

links.claim: The family screen reports greater in-vitro binding for the alternate T allele and names CTCF; its cited CTCF ChIP-seq peak is elsewhere, not at this variant.

critique.reason: E12 supports an alternate-allele in-vitro binding prediction, and E13 maps the candidate to CTCF. This is binding-prediction evidence, not direct occupancy at the variant; E13 places the CTCF peak elsewhere. The CTCF model is assessed as CTCF's own model.

regrade.reason: E12 reports greater in-vitro binding for the alternate allele and maps the model to CTCF, but this is a binding prediction, not evidence of occupancy at the variant in the stated cell type. E13 reports CTCF expression; E14 is not tested in the matched biosample and provides no evidence for or against binding there.

links.claim: The variant is intergenic and does not overlap a reported cCRE, so a regulatory element at this position is not established.

critique.reason: E01, E03 and E05 support the stated absence of an overlapping cCRE and that a regulatory element at this position is not established. This does not rule out regulatory activity outside the reported cCRE annotations.

regrade.reason: E03 and E05 directly report no overlapping cCRE, so a regulatory element is not established. However, E01 labels the consequence intron_variant while also reporting no transcript consequences, leaving the intergenic classification inconsistent.

links.claim: FAM110B is a tentative candidate: it is the nearest listed protein-coding gene by TSS and has literature search hits mentioning LDL, but the evidence does not link this variant to FAM110B regulation.

critique.reason: E02 makes FAM110B the nearest listed protein-coding gene by TSS, and E11 reports literature-search hits mentioning FAM110B and LDL. Neither links this variant to FAM110B regulation; the gene assignment remains speculative.

regrade.reason: E02 makes FAM110B the nearest listed protein-coding gene by TSS, but proximity and the literature search hits in E11 do not link the variant to FAM110B regulation. E15 reports no significant liver eQTL, which provides no support for that link.

links.claim: The supplied expression context is Hep 3B2.1-7; CTCF is reported at 32 TPM, but matched-biosample ChIP-seq support is absent.

critique.reason: E10 supplies Hep 3B2.1-7 as the expression context and E13 reports CTCF expression there. E12 reports no matched-biosample ChIP-seq support, so relevance of this cell type to binding at the variant is not established.

regrade.reason: E10 gives Hep 3B2.1-7 as the expression context and E13 reports CTCF expression there at 32 TPM. The claim correctly notes that matched-biosample ChIP-seq support is absent; E14 is not tested and does not count against it.

links.claim: No LDL-cholesterol mechanism or association is established by these data; the intake reports no association, and the GWAS Catalog search found none.

critique.reason: No positive evidence connects this variant or the proposed FAM110B mechanism to LDL cholesterol. E07 and E10 report no cataloged association, but the catalog result is weak negative evidence and does not establish absence of a causal effect.

regrade.reason: E07 and E10 report no listed LDL-cholesterol association, while E16 reports no FAM110B association with the specified large-LDL free-cholesterol measurement. These data do not establish an LDL-cholesterol mechanism or association for this chain.

predictions: If this hypothesis is correct, the T allele should show greater CTCF occupancy than G at the site in Hep 3B2.1-7; a downstream effect on FAM110B remains unsubstantiated.
falsified_if: Allele-specific occupancy assays in Hep 3B2.1-7 show no greater CTCF binding to T than G.
Variant perturbation or allele-specific assays provide no evidence of a regulatory effect on FAM110B.

problems: The CTCF evidence is an in-vitro binding prediction, not variant-site occupancy evidence in Hep 3B2.1-7.
No cCRE overlaps the variant, and E01's intron_variant label conflicts with its report of no transcript consequences; the element annotation needs reconciliation.
FAM110B is only a proximity-based candidate. No variant-to-FAM110B regulatory link is established, and the liver eQTL lookup was negative.
The provided evidence does not establish an LDL-cholesterol association or a disease mechanism for H1.
